exact_head_ci: WERK Parliamentary Trace Runtime Check #2 SUCCESS

findings.summary: The contract claims an append-only evidence trace and evidence-required transitions, but the live trace tables have no user triggers enforcing append-only/state-machine writes. service_role has UPDATE/DELETE privileges at runtime, and the trace table is explicitly writable, so an internal service-role write can change current_state/outcome fields or rewrite/delete event history without passing werk_advance_parliamentary_trace and its evidence checks. This breaches the stated data-integrity contract even though the tables are currently empty and external/public integration is disabled.
findings.required_reconciliation: Keep the existing parliamentary runtime lock/loop open and harden the existing tables/path so state changes and event history cannot bypass the controlled evidence transition path. No parallel trace system.

findings.summary: werk_create_parliamentary_trace implements SELECT-then-INSERT replay by source_decision_id/source_decision_version, but the live table has no UNIQUE constraint/index for that source tuple. Concurrent creates can therefore produce duplicate traces despite sequential replay tests passing.
findings.required_reconciliation: Add a database-level uniqueness/race-safe replay guard to the existing trace table/path and a concurrent regression test before countercheck.
